subject.title: [Bug] v2026.5.22 启动后 Gateway CPU 持续 100%+，导致请求延迟飙升 50-100 倍

question: Should normal Gateway startup continue to schedule provider-auth prewarm by default, or should startup prewarm become explicit opt-in while keeping auth-failure rewarm hooks active?
rationale: Current main can skip startup prewarm only through an explicit env-driven path, while normal startup still enables it; changing that default affects both startup responsiveness and eager provider-auth availability for existing users.

options.title: Make startup prewarm opt-in
options.body: Refresh and land the existing default-off PR so normal startup keeps the auth-failure rewarm hook but does not run the initial provider-auth sweep unless explicitly enabled.

options.title: Keep eager startup prewarm
options.body: Keep the current default only if maintainers accept the startup CPU/RPC tradeoff and document the env/doctor recovery path for affected users.

options.title: Require more live proof first
options.body: Ask for a current-main macOS or packaged Gateway before/after proof before changing the default, accepting that the issue remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Make startup prewarm opt-in
recommendation.body: Refresh and land the existing default-off PR so normal startup keeps the auth-failure rewarm hook but does not run the initial provider-auth sweep unless explicitly enabled.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored the open default-off maintainer PR and the live PR is the most concrete remaining implementation path.
